about.title: Westlake Village Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Westlake Village is a quiet Los Angeles County community, but defective products still cause serious harm here — whether it's a malfunctioning appliance in a home near Triunfo Canyon Road, a faulty vehicle part contributing to a crash along Agoura Road, or an unsafe tool used in a local garage or business. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person typically doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If a product hurt you or a family member in Westlake Village, preserving the item and documenting what occurred matters early on. whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each potentially share liability, which may widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: Because defect claims often hinge on physical evidence, preserving the product exactly as it was at the time of injury can matter more than in other injury cases.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability approach generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. An attorney can review your situation to determine which type of defect claim may apply.

items.question: I live near Lindero Canyon Road — does it matter where the injury happened?
items.answer: What matters most is where you purchased or used the product and where the injury occurred, which helps establish jurisdiction and evidence. Whether it happened near Lindero Canyon Road, Thousand Oaks Boulevard, or inside your home, an independent attorney can walk through the specific details with you.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, instructions, or parts, and avoid repairing or discarding it. This physical evidence is often central to proving a defect claim. An attorney in our network can advise on proper preservation once you're connected.
